bull.b: Very low leverage reduces fixed financial obligations and limits balance-sheet pressure while Chemomab advances its clinical programs. This provides more flexibility than a highly indebted structure, although continued losses still mean the company must manage its capital carefully.

The improvement in 2025 net losses indicates some expense discipline within the early-stage operating model. If maintained, lower losses could extend available resources and reduce financing pressure as the company works toward clinical milestones and eventual commercial progress.

Chemomab has a clearly defined scientific focus rather than a broad, unfocused pipeline. Concentrating on CCL24 and related fibro-inflammatory conditions can align research resources around a coherent mechanism and support continuity across its clinical development efforts.

bear.b: The absence of operating revenue means Chemomab has not yet demonstrated commercial traction or an internally funded business model. Its ability to create durable value therefore remains dependent on successful clinical development and eventual product approval and commercialization.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow indicates that research and corporate expenses continue to exceed internally generated funds. Continued dependence on external financing can constrain strategic flexibility and expose development plans to funding conditions over the next several quarters.

The planned U.S. redomiciliation and Scipher merger introduce several execution dependencies before the intended transaction can be completed. Regulatory, shareholder and financing requirements could delay the combination or alter its implementation, adding uncertainty to corporate planning and funding access.
